quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right, then look left again in case you missed any vehicles.

questions.question: Which medications could affect your ability to drive?
questions.correctAnswerText: Any medication
questions.explanation: Any medication could affect your driving ability. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about side effects. Read labels on over-the-counter medicines to see if they can impair your driving.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for traffic, then go if clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When driving near children playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run out in front of you without looking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed and use extra caution near children. They may not understand the danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected conditions.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you should:

options.text: Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases on:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet or icy roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads and on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: If you see an "Exit only" sign above your lane, you:

options.text: Can either continue through or exit from your lane.
Can stay in your lane and continue through.
Must exit if you stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit if you stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will leave the highway to form a ramp. You can change lanes to continue through the interchange, or you must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination quickly.
Decrease the distance between you and other cars.
Increase the distance between you and other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and other cars.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between you and other vehicles to allow more time to stop.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway. You see children playing nearby. What should you do before you start to move your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When you back up, look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially with children nearby. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.

questions.question: What color are signs that show areas of public recreation?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show areas of cultural, historical, or public recreation value. They help drivers find these places when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Then use your turn signal to show that you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that the area ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator sticks open while you are driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When your accelerator sticks, your vehicle will keep speeding up even if you remove your foot from the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully. Move only far enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, what can you do?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane to make that turn. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn your steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want to go. Once the vehicle begins to straighten out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: Can you legally drive 10 mph over the speed limit?
questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Speeding is against the law. You must obey the speed limit. There is no allowance to drive 10 mph over the limit. You are responsible for knowing and following the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay to the right of the upcoming divider.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT promote safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights causes your pupils to shrink. After the vehicle passes, your pupils need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this adjustment period, you cannot see clearly.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. You must slow down when roads are slippery or in poor condition to stay in control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, the driver of a small vehicle must be ready for:

options.text: Strong wind from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push small vehicles out of their lane. Be prepared to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in bad conditions.
The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
The suggested speed on a road in good conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but never faster. Slow down in school zones, work zones, and bad weather.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Does not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: On a road without sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Same side where traffic is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road facing the traffic nearest you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Turn left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns in the direction of the arrow. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must let them pass first, along with any pedestrians.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: An upcoming curve in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, first:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop next to the car in front of the space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: You have done all you need to do.
You must wait for the police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: When you hit a parked car, stop and try to find the owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about the accident.

questions.question: What is the first thing alcohol affects when you drink?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects all important driving skills, including judgment, reaction time, vision, and concentration. It enters your bloodstream and reaches your brain within minutes. Your judgment is affected first.

questions.question: Getting ____ points on your license in 36 months will result in your license being suspended for one year.
questions.correctAnswerText: 24 or more
questions.explanation: Certain driving violations add points to your license. If you get 24 or more points within 36 months, your license will be suspended for one year.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign tells you:

options.text: About dangerous conditions ahead on or near the road.
Which cities and towns are coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: About dangerous conditions ahead on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background. They warn you about conditions on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When another driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough space in front of your vehicle to complete their pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: When driving with poor visibility, you should:

options.text: Decrease the space between you and the car ahead.
Increase the space between you and the car ahead.
Drive as if visibility is good.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the space between you and other cars when visibility is poor. You need extra time to see and react to what the car ahead is doing.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in your car.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only make a brief stop to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or very near the road ahead. Drive carefully through work zones.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: If it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: You can park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway:

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the shoulder of a freeway except in an emergency.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press your brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Your first action when you cannot see well is to slow down. This is the best response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for one hour or more.
In the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. In hot weather, the heat makes even more oil rise to the surface, making roads even more slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This circular sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. Watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What happens if you let someone without a license drive your car?

options.text: 10 days in jail and a $100 fine.
30 days in jail and a $250 fine.
60 days in jail and a $500 fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: 60 days in jail and a $500 fine.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to let someone without a license drive your vehicle. You can be sentenced to 60 days in jail and fined $500. If the unlicensed driver causes an accident that injures or kills someone, your license will be suspended for one year.

questions.question: What can help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen because drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with others by using turn signals, honking your horn when needed, and giving warning signals when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When towing something behind your vehicle, what must be true about the towing connection?

options.text: It must be longer than 15 feet.
It must be strong enough to pull all the weight being towed.
It cannot have flags or reflectors on it.
It must have a yellow flag.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must be strong enough to pull all the weight being towed.
questions.explanation: Your towing connection must be strong enough to safely pull everything you are towing. If you use a rope, cable, or chain, attach a white flag that is 12 inches square. The towing connection should be no longer than 15 feet unless the towed object cannot be taken apart.

questions.question: What do highways use to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road.
White arrows in the middle of the lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes.
questions.explanation: White arrows painted in the lanes show drivers which lanes to use for driving straight or turning.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes if you can, so you do not drive next to the stopped vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Keep driving at the same speed in your lane.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes if you can, so you do not drive next to the stopped vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and change lanes if possible to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and stay as far away as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before turning left, where should you look?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
